children: , the cloud and enterprise-software giant, pulled back the curtain on Azureand the cloud engine is already a $100 billion monster. Azure produced $29.4 billion last quarter and $101.9 billion during the fiscal year ended June 30. The stock drops 1.6%, trading at $501.73 Friday.

Microsoft's annual results put total revenue at $331.8 billion, with $90 billion landing in the fourth quarter alone. Azure powered roughly 30.7% of annual revenue and 32.7% of quarterly sales. But investors will not get a perfectly clean view: Microsoft plans to house Azure inside Agents and Infra while moving some GitHub revenue into Microsoft 365 Cloud.

The new disclosure proves Azure has breathtaking scale, giving investors a direct measuring stick against Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud. What remains missing is just as important: Microsoft still does not reveal Azure's costs, operating margin or return on its huge infrastructure bet. At $501.73, the shares sit 13.75% below the $581.70 GF Value, creating a valuation gap investors cannot ignore.

title: Microsoft Drops 1.6%, Opens Azure's $101.9 Billion Door
